newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Rosgosstrakh privatisation seen going ahead.
newsitem.headline: Russia Rosgosstrakh privatisation seen going ahead.

text.p: The privatisation of Russia's largest insurer, Rosgosstrakh, will go ahead, although the scheme may change, a government spokeswoman said on Thursday.

"This is a planned privatisation and it will continue, although the implementation plan may be modified if it turns out to contravene existing legislation," the spokeswoman for First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin told Reuters.
The State Duma lower chamber of parliament on Wednesday urged the government to delay privatisation, planned for this year, until after March 10.

Under the current scheme, 50 per cent of the Rosgosstrakh shares will be sold by the Federal Property Fund at a cash auction and another 20 percent will be sold to workers who have priority for the final 30 percent.
Duma members say the current 2.13 billion rouble valuation of the national insurance company, calculated in 1993 without adjustment for subsequent hyperinflation, is too low.
They are waiting for Russia's Audit Chamber to present its own valuation of the company's assets.

The spokeswoman for Potanin, who heads the federal commission on revenues from privatisation, said Potanin had already asked government officials to examine whether the proposed privatisation scheme complied with federal law.
